extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, peer reviewers, and NIH extramural staff
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures used in NIH dual peer review (Scientific Review Groups and Advisory Councils) to evaluate research grant and cooperative agreement applications, including scoring, reviewer roles, review criteria, additional considerations, and post-review actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core values of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The core values of peer review drive the NIH to seek the highest level of ethical standards, and form the foundation for the laws, regulations, and policies that govern the NIH peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH policy is intended to promote a process whereby grant applications submitted to the NIH are evaluated on the basis of a process that strives to be fair, equitable, timely, and free of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual peer review system requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH dual peer review system is mandated by statute in accordance with section 492 of the Public Health Service Act and federal regulations governing 'Scientific Peer Review of Research Grant Applications and Research and Development Contract Projects'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first level of review is carried out by a Scientific Review Group (SRG). The second level is performed by Institute and Center (IC) National Advisory Councils or Boards. Only applications recommended for approval by both the SRG and the Advisory Council may be recommended for funding; final funding decisions are made by the IC Directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOA-specified review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Each FOA specifies all of the review criteria and considerations that will be used in the evaluation of applications submitted for that FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for Applications (RFAs) and certain Program Announcements may include additional review criteria and considerations; other funding opportunity types may use different review criteria. Unless the FOA specifies otherwise, standard NIH review procedures and the NIH scoring system are followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Officer (SRO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The SRO is the designated federal official responsible for ensuring that each application receives an objective and fair initial peer review, and that all applicable laws, regulations, and policies are followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SROs analyze the content of each application and check for completeness; document and manage conflicts of interest; recruit qualified reviewers considering authority in field, dedication to fair objective reviews, ability to work collegially, experience in grant review, and balanced representation; assign applications to reviewers for critique preparation and criterion scores; attend and oversee administrative and regulatory aspects of meetings; and prepare summary statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer recruitment qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are recruited based on scientific and technical qualifications and other considerations, including authority in their scientific field, dedication to high quality, fair, and objective reviews, ability to work collegially in a group setting, experience in research grant review, and balanced representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These recruitment factors guide SROs in selecting reviewers to ensure expertise and fair deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conflict of interest declaration and management
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must declare Conflicts of Interest with specific applications following NIH guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SROs document and manage conflicts of interest. Individuals with conflicts are not eligible to participate in scoring/discussion of the conflicted application; see Managing Conflict of Interest in NIH Peer Review of Grants and Contracts for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and integrity of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers receive access to grant applications approximately six weeks prior to the peer review meeting and must maintain the confidentiality of peer review information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must not contact reviewers, send information directly to reviewers, or access information related to the review; there are consequences for violating confidentiality and integrity rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer written critique and use of templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers prepare a written critique (using Review Critique Templates as directed by the Scientific Review Officer) for each application assigned, based on review criteria and judgment of merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crtiques form the basis of written reviewer feedback in the summary statement and should address the applicable review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer scoring of individual criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Each reviewer assigned to an application gives a separate score for each of (at least) five review criteria (Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach, and Environment for research grants and cooperative agreements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual scores of the assigned reviewers and discussant(s) for these criteria are reported to the applicant. Scores are given on the NIH 9-point rating scale (1 = exceptional; 9 = poor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer final impact score
rubrics_metrics.description: Each reviewer assigned to an application gives a preliminary overall impact score for that application before the SRG meeting and, for discussed applications, a final impact score during/after discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final overall impact score for each discussed application is determined by calculating the mean of all eligible members' final impact scores and multiplying by 10, yielding a reported range from 10 (high impact) to 90 (low impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall Impact is determined in consideration of the primary review criteria (Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach, Environment) and additional review criteria as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criteria — Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance (one of the scored review criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assign a numerical score for Significance as part of the set of at least five criterion scores that inform the overall impact score. (See Review Criteria at a Glance for full guidance.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criteria — Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator(s) (one of the scored review criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers score the qualifications, track record, and suitability of the investigators for the proposed work as part of the criterion scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criteria — Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation (one of the scored review criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers score the novelty and potential to shift current research paradigms as part of the criterion scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criteria — Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach (one of the scored review criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate the rigor, feasibility, and appropriateness of the proposed methods and analyses; assign a numerical Approach score that contributes to overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scored review criteria — Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment (one of the scored review criteria).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider institutional support, resources, and environment that will contribute to the project's success and score accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review criteria (not separately scored)
rubrics_metrics.description: As applicable for the project proposed, reviewers will evaluate the following additional items while determining scientific and technical merit and in providing an overall impact score, but will not give separate scores for these items: Protections for Human Subjects; Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children; Vertebrate Animals; Biohazards; Resubmission; Renewal; Revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items must be considered and addressed in reviewer comments and the overall impact assessment though they do not receive independent numeric criterion scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional review considerations (administrative and logistical factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: As applicable for the project proposed, reviewers will consider each of the following items, but will not give scores for these items and should not consider them in providing an overall impact score: Applications from Foreign Organizations; Select Agent; Resource Sharing Plans; Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources; Budget and Period Support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors are reviewed for completeness, compliance, and programmatic relevance but are not to be used in calculating the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH 9-point rating scale and scoring guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH utilizes a 9-point rating scale (1 = exceptional; 9 = poor) for all applications; the same scale is used for overall impact scores and for criterion scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary individual criterion and overall scores are given before the meeting; preliminary overall scores may be used to triage which applications are discussed. For discussed applications, each eligible member gives a final impact score; the mean of final impact scores is multiplied by 10 and reported (10–90). Applications not discussed are reported as ND (may be shown as ++ on the face page) and typically rank in the bottom half.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not Recommended for Further Consideration (NRFC) designation
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be designated Not Recommended for Further Consideration (NRFC) by the SRG if it lacks significant and substantial merit; presents serious ethical problems in the protection of human subjects from research risks; or presents serious ethical problems in the use of vertebrate animals, biohazards, and/or select agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRFC applications do not proceed to the second level of peer review (National Advisory Council/Board) because they cannot be funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary statement contents and ND designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that are not discussed at the meeting will be given the designation 'ND' (which may be reported as ++ on the face page of the summary statement); the applicant will see the written comments and scores from the assigned reviewers and discussants for each of the scored review criteria as feedback on their summary statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary statement will identify the base used to determine any reported percentile. Applicants receiving scores or summary statements should consult Next Steps guidance and may contact the NIH Program Official listed on the summary statement for additional advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentile reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: A percentile is the approximate percentage of applications that received a better overall impact score from the study section during the past year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All percentiles are reported as whole numbers. Only a subset of applications receive percentiles; the types of applications percentiled vary across Institutes and Centers. The summary statement will identify the base used to determine the percentile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for appeal of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH established a peer review appeal system to provide investigators and applicant organizations the opportunity to seek reconsideration of the initial review results if, after consideration of the summary statement, they believe the review process was flawed for reasons of either bias of a reviewer, conflict of interest, absence of appropriate expertise, or factual errors by one or more reviewers that could have substantially altered the review outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This appeals policy does not apply to appeals of the technical evaluation of R&D contract projects, appeals of NIH funding decisions, or appeals of decisions concerning extensions of MERIT award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-level review considerations (Advisory Council/Board)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Councils/Boards examine applications and consider the overall impact scores given during the peer review process, percentile rankings (if applicable) and the summary statements in light of the Institute/Center's priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff provide a grant-funding plan to the Council; Council members have access to applications and summary statements pending funding. Council members conduct Special Council Review for investigators receiving $1 million or more in direct costs to determine if additional funds should be provided. The Council advises the IC director, who makes final funding decisions based on staff and Council advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review options for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: If the original application is not funded, applicants may resubmit the application, making changes that address reviewer concerns, or they may submit a new application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are directed to the Next Steps guidance and may contact the NIH Program Official assigned to their application for guidance on resubmission and fundability. If an application results in an award, program and grants management staff will contact the applicant to arrange award preparation and administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paylines and fundable score guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Some ICs publish paylines as part of their funding strategies to guide applicants on their likelihood of receiving funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application scores can only be compared against the payline for the fiscal year when the application will be considered for funding. There may be delays at the beginning of fiscal years before paylines are determined. If the assigned IC does not announce a payline, the program official listed on the summary statement may provide guidance on the likelihood of funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant conduct regarding peer review integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must maintain the integrity of the peer review process by not contacting reviewers to influence the outcome of the review; not sending information directly to a reviewer; and not accessing information related to the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are consequences for such actions; see Integrity and Confidentiality in NIH Peer Review for specifics.
